chapter: Los Angeles scene in the 1930s and 40s
title: Bandleaders in Los Angeles in 1935
summary: She lists the Club Alabam band, C. L. Burke, Les Hite, Lloyd Reese and George Orendorff as the local bands when she arrived.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: When you got to Los Angeles in 1935, who were the people that were playing music here? Who were the people that you remember that had bands and were performing?

Well, the one person I remember -- I mean there were several. Lorenzo Flenoy, for instance, was at the Club Alabam. I think I mentioned this earlier. He was at the Club Alabam and he had about a 12 or 13 piece band. Some of the guys that were with him are still around. Lorenzo's passed on since that time. He had guys like Buddy Harper and Red Mack and Bradley. I can't think --

Oscar Bradley. And -- funny, I can't remember the other guys, isn't it funny, offhand. It'll come to me. But then you had C. L. Burke, he was around. You had I think C. L. Burke had the band out at the place called the Bell Tavern at that time. They had shows. And of course Les Hite was out at the Cotton Club with a big band, and then that band was Peppy Prince who's still around. Peppy was the drummer for them and also doing vocalizing. A very fine vocalist and drummer. And you had -- let's see, who else was -- oh, Lloyd Reese, who's gone on. Lloyd Reese was a very marvelous

trumpeter. Lloyd's gone. Then you had George Orendorff. George Orendorff is still around, a very fine trumpet player. And -- I can't remember the other guys, offhand, but quite a few of the guys are still around, the older guys.
And those were the people who you remember best as being --

They were the musicians. And of course earlier I did mention guys like Sylvester Scott, who was at the Breakfast Club. He was the piano player for, oh, all of the people who worked at the Breakfast Club.

At the Club Alabam. And you had people like Ned Stanfield, who was a piano player. Ned Stanfield was around here when I first came here, and he later went back into the profession. He's a doctor, and he played around Los Angeles in some of the spots as a single, you know. And also you have people like Dudley Brooks, Eddie Beal. These people were all here when I first came here. And Fred Skinner, who's another man who was quite a big -- who was quite a big name and a very popular local talent when I first came here. He was working at the Ambassador, would you believe that.
